candidates.text:
I have a genuine question.

Anthropic has probably been working on Fable 5.1 for a very long time. OpenAI has probably been working on GPT-6 Astra for just as long. These labs are almost certainly building in parallel, not reacting to each other in real time of course.

So why does Fable 5.1 launch just a couple of days before Astra, and then Astra beats it on almost every benchmark by a good margin?

And this isn't a one-off.

Every single launch follows the same pattern: when Anthropic ships a new model, it beats all of OpenAI's previous models.
When OpenAI ships a new model, it beats all of Anthropic's previous models. Now they are actually beating what the other just launched days earlier.

Benchmarks are completely vanity metrics.

candidates.text:
Lots of confusion about the 13 million LOC.

Mathematics was historically brittle because a hard proof could fall to crumbles because of a tiniest slip in a minor result.

The whole effort of formalization was to make a kernel stable (Lean) and build the proofs around it.

*If* Lean has no issues then mathematicians don't need to read all the minutae of a proof, and the number 13 millions loc doesn't matter.

Another way to think of this. With 13M loc you either have a proof of your theorem, or a hack of the Lean system. Those do exist, this August OpenAI found 6 bugs in Lean https://t.co/gQaiLLKbOH but as the system matures it gets hardened and hardened.

I'm calling 26th of August AI Independence Day.

DeepSeekV4-Flash was the first frontier-adjacent model you could squeeze onto a Spark. Now Qwen3.8-Flash-Next fits in under $5K of hardware, and GLM5.3 fits with some pruning.

The intuition I've been trying to communicate for a while is that total size decides whether you can run it, while active size decides whether it's pleasant to use. Both numbers are finally landing in a good place at the same time. 

Which means: unlimited tokens at home.

In this week's posts I chat about Flash models, and ox-alpha, the undercover model that was doxxed:
